# Resources

## Get On Gopher Slack

We use a slack channel to share links, code, and examples during the training.  This is free. This is also the same slack community you will use after training to ask for help and interact with may Go experts around the world in the community.

Using the following link, fill out your name and email address:

1. [https://invite.slack.golangbridge.org/](https://invite.slack.golangbridge.org/)
1. Check your email, and follow the link to the slack application.
1. Join the training channel by clicking on this link:
	[https://gophers.slack.com/messages/gopherguides/](https://gophers.slack.com/messages/gopherguides/)
1. Click the “Join Channel” button at the bottom of the screen.

## Join Your Local Go Meetup!

There are go meetups all around the world.  A great place to find them is on [meetup.com](http://meetup.com).

Here are all the [go related meetups world wide](https://www.meetup.com/find/?allMeetups=false&keywords=golang&radius=Infinity&userFreeform=Sunnyvale%2C+CA&mcId=z94086&mcName=Sunnyvale%2C+CA&sort=recommended&eventFilter=mysugg).

You can also find more information on the [go wiki](https://github.com/golang/go/wiki#the-go-community).

## Go Playgound

Many of the code examples in this presentation can be run on the Go Playground.

This is a great way to share code samples, solutions, or problems with other developers as well.

[Go Playground](http://play.golang.org)
